  "options": [
    "A. The proposer may choose an arbitrary new value as long as n is larger than every proposal number seen in the PREPARE responses.",
    "B. The proposer must receive responses from a majority quorum, and if any response indicates a previously accepted proposal, it must propose the value associated with the highest-numbered accepted proposal seen; if none is indicated, it may propose an arbitrary value.",
    "C. The proposer must wait until every acceptor responds to PREPARE(n) before it can decide, because a non-responding acceptor might have accepted a higher-numbered proposal.",
    "D. The proposer can ignore previously accepted values if its own proposal number n is strictly greater than all accepted proposal numbers reported by the quorum."
  ],
  "correct_answer": "B",
  "explanation": "Paxos safety depends on quorum intersection and the invariant that once a value is accepted, no higher-numbered proposal may choose a different value. A proposer must hear from a majority quorum; if any member of that quorum has accepted a proposal, the proposer must adopt the value with the highest proposal number among those accepted values. It only has freedom to choose an arbitrary value when no accepted value was reported by the responding quorum. It does not need responses from all acceptors, and it cannot override an already accepted value merely because its own proposal number is larger."
